use_case: Automated video analysis and predictive maintenance
summary: Project Maven is a foundational DoD effort that leverages general-purpose AI/ML, primarily computer vision, to automate intelligence analysis from full-motion video and has expanded to include predictive maintenance and other operational support functions.
description: Launched in April 2017, Project Maven was a foundational DoD effort to accelerate the integration of big data, AI, and machine learning into its programs. Its initial objective was to automate the processing, exploitation, and dissemination (PED) of full-motion video (FMV) collected by intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) assets, primarily using computer vision algorithms for object detection, classification, and alerts. This involved bringing industry-best software in AI and computer vision to FMV, fielding it to warfighters, gathering feedback, and rapidly upgrading the tools' performance. While initially focused on FMV analysis for counterinsurgency and counterterrorism operations, its scope quickly expanded to include broader applications such as predictive maintenance for aircraft (e.g., for the Army's 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment), cybersecurity, and even monitoring special operators' brain health. The project faced early challenges, including data fragmentation and issues with algorithm accuracy (around 50% for geo-referencing), which led to the adoption of a 'field to learn' approach and the development of new human-machine interfaces to improve utility. By Spring 2018, significant progress was reported, with AI acting as a 'combat multiplier' by freeing human analysts to focus on more complex tasks. Project Maven was explicitly identified as a key 'National Mission Initiative' for the newly established Joint Artificial Intelligence Center (JAIC).

use_case: AI-enhanced battlefield command and operational planning, achieving "intelligentization"
summary: The PLA is strategically integrating general-purpose AI, including LLMs, into battlefield decision-making processes, aiming for "intelligentization" through phased development from human augmentation to AI-dominated command.
description: The concept of 'intelligentization' is central to China's military reforms and its ambition to become a 'world-class military' by 2049. The PLA views artificial intelligence as indispensable for processing the enormous and increasing amounts of data from various battlefield sensors, thereby enhancing situational awareness and dramatically accelerating commanders' decision-making. Articles published in the PLA Daily in 2023 outline a phased approach to integrating AI into military decision-making. In the initial phase, AI, including Large Language Models trained on historical war cases, will augment human decision-making by providing insights during pre-combat mission analysis. The second phase envisions AI capable of generating reconnaissance, firing, and complete operational plans based on commander guidance. The ultimate third phase anticipates AI dominating battlefield decision-making throughout the entire process, from planning to combat implementation.

use_case: Facial recognition for identification of combatants, collaborators, and displaced persons
summary: Clearview AI reportedly provided its facial recognition database to Ukrainian authorities, which used it to identify hundreds of thousands of individuals tied to the conflict.
description: Reporting indicates Clearview AI made its facial-recognition tool available to numerous Ukrainian offices and officials, enabling identification of alleged Russian soldiers, collaborators, and missing persons. The deployment has raised privacy and human-rights concerns given broad, wartime use of invasive biometric tools.

use_case: Procurement of AI-enabled ISR and targeting systems
summary: Israel’s Ministry of Defense contracted Elbit and Rafael for AI-enabled ISR drones and targeting platforms in 2024–2025.
description: Elbit Systems and Rafael, Israel’s leading defense contractors, have active deals with the Ministry of Defense for supplying ISR drones, targeting systems, and other AI-capable military technologies. These procurements represent ongoing integration of AI into Israel’s military.

use_case: Signals-intelligence, data fusion, and decision-support
summary: Unit 8200, Israel’s SIGINT arm, has been central in developing AI tools for intelligence, targeting and decision-support, with many linked to reported systems like Lavender and Gospel.
description: Unit 8200, known as Israel’s high-tech intelligence hub, has conducted R&D on AI tools for data analysis and targeting. Many investigative reports trace the origins of operational AI systems such as Lavender and Gospel to this unit.

project: AI-enabled drone ISR and strike support
use_case: ISR, target tracking, and strike support with UAVs
summary: Israeli forces used AI-assisted drones for ISR and strike support in Gaza, with companies like Elbit and Rafael supplying AI-enabled UAV platforms.
description: During operations in Gaza, Israel deployed drones for ISR and strike coordination, with AI components aiding image processing, target triage, and real-time decision-making. Defense industry sources confirm Elbit and Rafael contracts for such AI-capable systems.

use_case: Locating individuals for time-sensitive strikes
summary: Reported AI tool nicknamed 'Where’s Daddy?' used to locate suspected Palestinian fighters in their homes for strikes during Israel's invasion of the Gaza.
description: According to investigative reporting, 'Where’s Daddy?' was integrated into IDF’s targeting ecosystem to track suspected Palestinians' home routines, enabling strikes when individuals were present. The families of these suspects were often present during the attacks, which raises questions about proportionality and AI-driven surveillance.

use_case: AI-assisted target generation for structures and facilities
summary: The Gospel system, reported as an AI platform, was said to generate and prioritize targets for airstrikes, dramatically increasing the number of targets produced compared to human analysts alone.
description: Gospel (Habsora) has been described as a platform capable of scanning data streams and suggesting targets for strikes. Reports claim it automated parts of the IDF’s strike planning, raising concerns about speed, accountability, and civilian harm.

sources.title: Israel’s AI targeting systems: ‘The Gospel’ and ‘Lavender’
Inside Israel’s AI war machine

use_case: AI-assisted individual-target identification
summary: Investigative reports allege the IDF deployed an AI system called Lavender that indexed tens of thousands of Palestinians as suspected militants to generate strike recommendations.
description: Lavender reportedly cross-references telecom, social and imagery data to identify individuals for targeting lists. Investigations by +972 Magazine and The Guardian suggested it played a major role in target generation post-October 7, 2023. The IDF disputes some characterizations, but multiple sources corroborate its existence and operational role. Its use raises several important questions about Israel's violation of international humanitarian principles
